court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Sau. Manjiri Prashant Bhokardankar v. Dr. Prashant Sakharam Bhokardankar
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage solemnized in 2005, dispute arose, wife started residing with mother at Amravati, husband filed for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, wife also filed domestic violence and maintenance proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to establish that it is difficult for her to attend the proceedings at Sangamner.
legal_principles.held: After hearing learned counsel for the applicant, I have perused the application as well as documents filed on record. It appears that due to dispute with her husband started residing with her mother at Amravati.
use_in: divorce cases where parties are physically far apart

legal_principles.principle: A court may consider the practical difficulties faced by a party in attending proceedings at a distant location.
legal_principles.held: It is difficult for applicant to attend the proceedings at Sangamner which is more than 500 Km.
use_in: cases involving distant locations or logistical challenges

outcome.final_order: Application allowed due to difficulty in attending proceedings at Sangamner which is more than 500 km away from Amravati.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
